_comment: Prose claims that something DOES NOT EXIST in the corpus. `absence_audit.py` re-runs each registered search and fails if it now matches. Registering an absence claim WITHOUT a search that could falsify it is the anti-pattern this registry exists to discourage -- a claim nothing can refute is not checked, it is merely written down.

claim_text: there is no other way to write a constant at this layer
claims.note: MachLib.Real carries OfNat for 0 and 1 only (Basic.lean:38-39). This is why numerals must be written as natCast N, which is the single most repeated tactic gotcha in the corpus. Verified: exactly 2 OfNat Real instances at registration. NOTE ON THE PATTERN: it first used a negative lookahead `(?!Zero|One)`, which grep -E does not support (POSIX ERE has none), so it matched instOfNatOne and reported a false NOW-FALSE. That failure was LOUD. The dangerous direction is the opposite one -- a search too NARROW to match anything passes silently, and nothing in this auditor detects it.

example (a c : MachLib.Real) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    (0 : MachLib.Real) - a / c = (0 - a) / c := by
  rw [MachLib.Real.neg_div hc]

claims.note: TERM-MISMATCH probe. This corpus writes negation as `0 - ·` throughout (`psub`, `pscale (0-1)`), so `neg_div` -- stated over `-(_)` -- does not fire on the goals it looks applicable to, and a backward `rw` against `= 0` finds the zero INSIDE `0 - _`. The second cost a 200 000-heartbeat timeout on 2026-09-09. If a `0 - ·` form of `neg_div` is ever added, this probe compiles and the note should be updated. Source file updated 2026-09-10 when the RatGerm algebra was split out of LogGermAssembly — the audit caught the move as TEXT-GONE rather than passing, which is the decay it exists to detect.

claim_text: nothing but `real_fpfinite` and `real_round_finite` concludes that a float is finite from premises that assume none
no axiom but those two and `real_exp_finite`, `real_sinh_finite`, `real_cosh_finite` and `real_log_finite` concludes that a float is finite

probe.snippet:
open Lean Meta Elab Command in
#eval show CommandElabM Unit from do
  let env ← getEnv
  let fin := ``Float.isFinite
  -- S: `Float.isFinite`, and every inductive with a constructor argument whose CONCLUSION mentions a member
  -- of S (so `FloatSafe` and `FPFiniteOfRange` are in S; `FPBridgeFinite` is not: it only assumes finiteness).
  let inds := env.constants.toList.filterMap fun (n, ci) =>
    match ci with | .inductInfo v => some (n, v.ctors) | _ => none
  let mut S : NameSet := NameSet.empty.insert fin
  let mut changed := true
  while changed do
    changed := false
    for (n, ctors) in inds do
      if !S.contains n then
        let mut stores := false
        for c in ctors do
          if let some cci := env.find? c then
            let hit ← liftTermElabM <| forallTelescope cci.type fun xs _ => do
              let mut h := false
              for x in xs do
                let t ← inferType x
                let tc ← forallTelescope t fun _ b => pure b
                if tc.getUsedConstants.any S.contains then h := true
              return h
            if hit then stores := true
        if stores then
          S := S.insert n
          changed := true
  -- Part 1. A producer: an axiom or theorem whose conclusion mentions `Float.isFinite` (or, for an axiom, any member of
  -- S), none of whose premises' conclusions mention a member of S.
  let mut producers : Array Name := #[]
  -- Part 2. Every AXIOM whose conclusion mentions a member of S, whatever its premises assume.
  let mut concluders : Array Name := #[]
  for (n, ci) in env.constants.toList do
    let kind : Option Bool := match ci with
      | .axiomInfo _ => some true | .thmInfo _ => some false | _ => none
    if let some isAx := kind then
      if ci.type.getUsedConstants.any S.contains then
        let (ok, concl) ← liftTermElabM <| forallTelescope ci.type fun xs body => do
          let bc := body.getUsedConstants
          let concl := isAx && bc.any S.contains
          unless bc.contains fin || (isAx && bc.any S.contains) do return (false, concl)
          for x in xs do
            let t ← inferType x
            let tc ← forallTelescope t fun _ b => pure b
            if tc.getUsedConstants.any S.contains then return (false, concl)
          return (true, concl)
        if ok then producers := producers.push n
        if concl then concluders := concluders.push n
  -- The range axioms are producers by design, and the libm finiteness axioms (2026-09-14) conclude finiteness from a
  -- finite input. The scan must SEE each of the six (one that cannot is broken, and must not read as a pass).
  let range : Array Name := #[``Certcom.real_fpfinite, ``Certcom.real_round_finite]
  let libm : Array Name := #[``Certcom.real_exp_finite, ``Certcom.real_sinh_finite, ``Certcom.real_cosh_finite,
    ``Certcom.real_log_finite]
  for a in range do
    unless producers.contains a do
      throwError m!"SCAN-BROKEN: the range axiom {a} is not seen as a finiteness producer"
  for a in range ++ libm do
    unless concluders.contains a do
      throwError m!"SCAN-BROKEN: {a} is not seen as an axiom concluding finiteness"
  let mut others : Array Name := #[]
  for n in producers do
    unless range.contains n do
      let axs ← Lean.collectAxioms n
      unless range.any axs.contains do
        others := others.push n
  let otherAxioms := concluders.filter fun n => !((range ++ libm).contains n)
  if others.isEmpty && otherAxioms.isEmpty then
    throwError "NO-OTHER-FINITENESS-PRODUCER: nothing but real_fpfinite and real_round_finite concludes that a float is finite from premises that assume none, and no other axiom concludes it at all"
  else
    logInfo m!"finiteness producers not resting on the range axioms: {others}; other axioms concluding finiteness: {otherAxioms}"

claims.note: ENVIRONMENT probe. Registered on 2026-09-14 as `no-float-finiteness-producer` ('no theorem or axiom here concludes that a float is finite'), narrowed the same day when the owner approved the range axioms `real_fpfinite` and `real_round_finite`, and narrowed again, still the same day, for the libm finiteness axioms `real_exp_finite`, `real_sinh_finite`, `real_cosh_finite` and `real_log_finite`. Part 1 is the original scan: every axiom and theorem after `import MachLib` that concludes Float.isFinite (or, for an axiom, an inductive that stores finiteness, such as a structure whose field concludes it) from premises that supply none; only the two range axioms, and theorems whose `#print axioms` footprint includes one of them, may be found. The libm axioms take a finite input, so Part 1 cannot see them at all, and the sentence it guarded would have gone on reading as true of a corpus with four more axioms concluding finiteness. Part 2 closes that: every AXIOM whose conclusion mentions finiteness, whatever its premises assume, must be one of the six by name. It throws SCAN-BROKEN if it does not see all six, so a scan that stopped working reads as broken rather than as a pass. Checked capable of both verdicts before this change was committed (see the commit): it throws NO-OTHER-FINITENESS-PRODUCER on the corpus and on a planted theorem resting on `real_round_finite`; it finds a planted axiom concluding a literal finite, a planted axiom carrying finiteness from a finite input to `Float.sin`, and it throws SCAN-BROKEN when told to expect `real_tanh_rounds`. If it fires, a finiteness fact that none of the six supplies has arrived, and what_is_proven.md's grounded-certificates lane and the Grounded*Instances docstrings must be revisited.

#eval show IO Unit from do
  if (← System.FilePath.pathExists "axiom_ledger.json") then
    IO.println "axiom_ledger.json is present"
  else
    throw <| IO.userError "axiom-ledger-json-absent: foundations/axiom_ledger.json does not exist"

claims.note: FILE probe. The claim is that a generated snapshot is gone, which a search cannot state: run_search greps *.lean only. The harness runs `lake env lean` from foundations/, so the relative path is foundations/axiom_ledger.json, and the snippet throws, naming this id, only when that file is absent; a file that comes back makes the probe COMPILE and read NOW-FALSE. Both verdicts were run through absence_audit.run_probe at registration: (clean, saw) = (True, False) with the file present, then (False, True) after `git rm`. The file went because nothing read it and it had drifted (220 in its own scope against a live 224, while the ledger pinned 256, all measured 2026-09-15). If this fires, whoever brought it back must name what reads it and gate it against the ledger, or delete it again.
